record.paper_title: (E,E′N) and (E,E′NN) Experiments at NIKHEF, Mainz and JLab and Open Problems in One- and Two-Nucleon Emissions
record.original_question: How can the two-hole spectral density for proton-neutron knockout be determined accurately enough to disentangle tensor-correlation effects from the large and complicated contributions of meson-exchange and other two-body currents in exclusive (e,e′pn) reactions? In superparallel kinematics the predicted (e,e′pn) cross sections are strongly enhanced, but the open problem is to separate how much of that enhancement comes from tensor correlations and how much comes from two-body current mechanisms.

evidence.quote: Tensor correlations are expected to play a major role in (e,e′pn) reactions where, however, the proton-neutron pair is ejected by a much more complicated mechanism involving two-body currents.
This enhancement is partly due to meson-exchange currents and partly to tensor correlations.
An accurate determination of the two-hole spectral density is thus most desirable in order to disentangle the effects of two-body currents from those of nuclear correlations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the exclusive electron-induced two-nucleon knockout reaction $A(e,e'pn)B$ on a nuclear target, in which an incident electron scatters off a nucleus, transferring four-momentum $(\omega,\mathbf{q})$ via a virtual photon, and a proton-neutron pair is detected in coincidence with the scattered electron in the final state, leaving a residual nucleus $B$ in a discrete or low-lying state. The cross section receives contributions from:

(i) one-body currents acting on a correlated proton-neutron pair described by the two-hole spectral density $S_{pn}(\mathbf{p}_1,\mathbf{p}_2;E)$, in which short-range and tensor nucleon-nucleon correlations in the initial state allow the pair to absorb the virtual photon; and

(ii) two-body currents, including meson-exchange currents and isobar ($\Delta$) currents, which can excite a proton-neutron pair directly.

In the so-called superparallel kinematics, in which both ejected nucleons are detected along the direction of the momentum transfer $\mathbf{q}$ (one parallel and one antiparallel), theoretical calculations predict a substantial enhancement of the $(e,e'pn)$ cross section relative to the $(e,e'pp)$ cross section.

Problem. Devise an experimental and/or theoretical procedure (for example, a choice of kinematics, observables, or polarization degrees of freedom, together with a determination of the proton-neutron two-hole spectral density of sufficient accuracy) that allows one to separate quantitatively the contribution of ground-state tensor correlations from the contribution of two-body meson-exchange and isobar currents to the exclusive $(e,e'pn)$ cross section, so that the predicted enhancement in superparallel kinematics can be unambiguously attributed to its two physical origins.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (including 12C(e,e'pN) short-range correlation measurements and ongoing studies of two-body currents in lepton-nucleus reactions) continues to address the interplay between tensor correlations and meson-exchange/two-body currents, indicating that a clean disentanglement in exclusive (e,e'pn) reactions remains an active research problem rather than a settled one.

status_evidence.title: 12C(e,e'pN) measurements of short range correlations in the tensor-to-scalar interaction transition region
status_evidence.snippet: High missing-momentum protons belong to short-ranged correlated pairs; data consistent with transition from tensor-dependent NN interaction at ~400 MeV/c to scalar interaction at ~800 MeV/c.
status_evidence.claim: Tensor vs. scalar SRC contributions are still being mapped experimentally in (e,e'pN) reactions.

status_evidence.title: Interference between Meson Exchange and One-Body Currents in Quasielastic Electron Scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies interference of meson-exchange and one-body currents in electron scattering.
status_evidence.claim: Separating two-body current effects from correlation effects remains an active topic.

status_evidence.title: Impact of Two-Body Currents on Semi-Exclusive Lepton-Nucleus Reactions
status_evidence.snippet: Ongoing comparisons of two-body current effects in spectral function vs. Fermi gas models.
status_evidence.claim: Two-body current contributions in exclusive/semi-exclusive lepton-nucleus reactions are still being quantified.
